messages.body_plain:

I have been using the GGIR package for a statistical project and after running my raw data, this message appears:

cannot allocate vector of size 465.0 Mb

Does that mean the computer I use for my project does not have enough memory to process all of the data the GENEActiv watch collected?

Thank you very much for your help,

Celia Kingsbury

messages.body_plain:

I just want to make sure I understand the argument loglocation. It is the location of a speadsheet (csv) with the sleep info reported by the watch user that the GGIR package will use in its analysis to improve the sleep estimations? If this is it, how does it work?

Thank you,

Celia Kingsbury

messages.subject: Re: loglocation= "C:/mydata/sleeplog.csv"
messages.body_plain:
Hi Celia,

Yes, that's correct, loglocaiton refers to the path to a csv with the reported sleep times. You should indicate the column in which your identicator variable is (argument: "colid"), as well as the column that contains the sleep onset hour for the first night (argument: "coln1"). From this column, your csv should include all the sleep onset and waking-up times in this order: sleep onset 1, waking.up time 1, sleep onset 2, waking up time 2,....

You can find an example here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#output-part-4 (2.4.5 loglocation)

Hope this helps.

Jairo

messages.subject: Re: Difficulties regarding Part 4
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom,

First, try by changing the "includenightcrit" argument, you are asking for 16 valid hours during night to consider it, and it is very unlikely. Try with 4 as default in the function. Then, if you are not going to use diary, just remove the path to your dummy log and remove the arguments "colid" and "coln1". If you want to use the sleeplog, "colid" should be 1, and "coln1" should be 2 (following the structure of the log that you have attached). Finally, I suggest you to change the argument "relayonsleeplog" to FALSE, either if you are using sleeplog or not.

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Difficulties regarding Part 4
messages.body_plain:
Jairo wrote: "First, try by changing the "includenightcrit" argument, you are asking for 16 valid hours during night to consider it, and it is very unlikely."
No, this advise is incorrect. The window is defined from noon to noon, so 16 hours allows for 8 hours of nonwear time in a day, which I think is already high. I would nog advise lowering the 16 if your interest lies in sleep variables. 16 was inspired by traditional literature where 2/3 of the instructed wear duration should reflect useful data (10 out of 15 hours). Considering that modern studies have a 24 hour protocol the equivalent criteria then becomes 16 hours of required wear time per day. I think this is too soft, but I set it as a default to at least make sure users do not stick to the even worse 10 hours in the literature that had a daytime only wear protocol.
Best, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Difficulties regarding Part 4
messages.body_plain:
So, I think the definition provided in the help material of "g.part4" should be clarified. The information about this argument states: "Minimum number of valid hours per night (24 hour window between noon and noon)". If it is based in 24 hours, it should not state "per night". Also, in the Usage section of this same help material, it is set "includenightcrit" as 4 by default, not 16. And then, what is the difference between this argument and "includedaycrit"? We can find both arguments together in "g.report.part5", I interpreted this as minimum valid hours required during night, and during day, respectively to consider a valid day.
Best,
Jairo
